name: The Sapiegos Park Linden

location.address: Sapiegos Park, Antakalnio gatve, near the entrance gates of Sapiegos Palace, Antakalnis

access: Free, in the public Sapiegos Park (Sapiegos rumu parkas), open to visitors
transport: Antakalnis district, about 2.2 km from the Old Town cluster; reachable by city bus
verify_notes: Vilnius's oldest recorded linden, protected as a municipal botanical nature heritage object since 29 May 1996 (register id 0310505050028, 'Seniausia liepa'). Two-trunked veteran, trunk circumference 4.40 m at 1.3 m height, originally 28 m tall. On 18 July 2023 a storm broke the tree: an arborist found it 'completely rotten' inside and improperly pruned in the past, leaving a top-heavy crown that acted as a lever in the wind. The remaining trunk is roughly 11 to 12 m tall. Sources agree the tree survived and was expected to regrow from dormant lower buds ('it will not live another 300 years, but our grandchildren might see new growth'), and it was entered as a candidate in Lithuania's Tree of the Year 2023 competition after the storm, which independently confirms it was still standing and recognised post-damage. FLAGGED because the most recent detailed condition report found is from 2023 (over two years old): confirm current standing/regrowth before publishing confidently, and the story should be honest that this is a storm-damaged veteran rather than an intact 28 m tree. Age is the register/Wikipedia figure (~300-350 years, sources vary slightly); no growth-rate calculation was needed since a documented age already exists. Girth recorded pre-storm; may have changed with the loss of the upper trunk. Stands alone, 2.2 km from the Old Town cluster (Bernardinai Garden group), so it starts a second, single-tree point rather than joining a walk.

name: The Pine of Kalnai Park

location.address: Kalnai Park (Kalnu parkas), southwestern slope of Dainu slenis (Vilnius Song Valley), behind the amphitheatre spectator stands

verified_sources: register: data/registers/lithuania-stvk-gpo.json, register_id 0310505020044, name_lt 'Kalnu parko pusis'
access: Free, in the public Kalnai Park (the Song Valley amphitheatre park), open at all times
transport: About 1.3 km from the Old Town cluster (Bernardinai Garden); walkable, views over the Old Town
verify_notes: Named individually in the register as 'Kalnu parko pusis' and confirmed as a real, municipality-protected tree by the Lithuanian Wikipedia article on Kalnu parkas, which lists it among the park's named heritage trees ('Kalnu parko pusis - savivaldybes saugomas medis'). A separate web search surfaced a description of a 'more than 150-year-old two-stemmed Scots pine' on the park's southwestern slope behind the amphitheatre stands, but I could not confirm that specific age/stem-count claim against a primary document within the time budget, so age_estimate is left EMPTY rather than repeating an unverified figure; flag for a reader or a later pass to confirm on the ground. location_precision is approximate: the register coordinate is tile-rounded per the register's own caveat and I found no tree-level survey coordinate or photo to sharpen it, though the park is small enough that the pin lands within the right area. Kalnai Park is the public Song Valley park with views over the Old Town, free and open. Two independent sources for existence and species (register + Wikipedia article); no second source yet for age, so age stays unset rather than guessed.

name: The Amur Cork Trees and Crimean Linden of Bernardinai Garden
species: Amur Cork Tree (Phellodendron amurense) and Crimean Linden (Tilia x euchlora)

location.address: Bernardinai Garden (Sereikiskes Park / Bernardinu sodas), Old Town

verified_sources: register: data/registers/lithuania-stvk-gpo.json, register_id 0310506000020, name_lt 'Bernardinu sodo medziu grupe'
access: Free, in the public Bernardinai Garden, the same park as the city's other four shipped trees (vln_001, vln_005, vln_006, vln_007)
transport: Old Town, inside the existing 0.7 km Bernardinai Garden walk
verify_notes: Register entry 'Bernardinu sodo medziu grupe' (Bernardinai garden tree group) is named in the Lithuanian Wikipedia article on Bernardinu sodas as 'Medziu grupe (dvieju Amuro kamsteniu ir Krymo liepos grupe)': a group of two Amur cork trees (Phellodendron amurense) and one Crimean linden (Tilia x euchlora), one of the park's named 1996 municipal heritage designations, alongside the already-shipped oldest oak, nine-trunked willow, four-trunked linden and three-trunked ash. This is a genuinely distinctive, named composition (two of one species plus one of another), not a generic 'group of trees', so it clears the collectible-point bar the way the earlier-blocked generic groups in this same park did not. FLAGGED and evidence is thin: the Wikipedia mention and the register entry likely trace back to the same underlying 1996 municipal resolution rather than being truly independent, so treat this as ONE source for now; no age, girth or individual measurements found anywhere. No dedicated article or photo found to pin the exact spot within the park, hence approximate precision; it sits inside the already-published 0.7 km Bernardinai Garden cluster, so it joins the existing walk rather than starting a new one. A reader on the ground could confirm the exact spot and species reading easily.
